I am 72 years old and have been farming this land in Mangochi all my life. This small plot of beans is important for my family's food, but I save any fertilizer coupons I receive for my maize plot because beans can draw nitrogen from the air. I keep my own bean seed from last season's harvest — it has served me well for many years, and I do not trust these new varieties that come and go. My children and grandchildren will provide the labor for planting, weeding, and harvesting; at my age, I supervise and do what light work I can, but I do not have money to hire outside workers. We rely on the rains that God provides, and I do not spray chemicals on food crops because they cost too much at the market.
